thread.title: Netflix Stock Rises As Analyst Turns Positive After Being On Fence

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Netflix Stock Rises As Analyst Turns Positive After Being On Fence

organizations.name: netflix stock rises as analyst turns positive after being on fence netflix

text:
Netflix stock rose Friday after a Wall Street analyst turned positive on the internet television provider after being on the sidelines.
X SunTrust Robinson Humphrey analyst Matthew Thornton upgraded Netflix ( NFLX ) to buy from hold, though he trimmed his price target to 410 from 415.
Netflix stock surged 5.8% to 358.82 on the stock market today . It had tumbled 22% over several weeks after reporting disappointing second-quarter subscriber gains on July 16 . It bottomed at 310.93 on Monday before starting to rebound this week.
Thornton upgraded the stock based on its recent pullback and because of data indicating solid subscriber gains ahead.

Please contact customer service CLOSE His data pointed to domestic and international subscribers "solidly in-line to ahead" of views for the third quarter. Consensus estimates for the fourth quarter look "reasonable," he said in a report to clients.
Netflix India Shows Create Buzz In India, Netflix's first array of original series there appear to be "resonating quite well," boosting interest in the streaming video service. Those shows include "Sacred Games" and "Ghoul."
"We see potential catalysts around additional partnerships (particularly in India) and tactical price increases (recent increases in Japan)," Thornton said.
He added, "Bigger picture, we continue to see opportunity around IP (intellectual property) licensing for consumer products/services (still early) and content licensing (currently China only) and long-term optionality around pricing points (India), product placement, box office, and even password sharing (Blockchain)."
Bypassing The App Stores Recent moves by Netflix to bypass mobile app stores and avoid paying commissions to Apple ( AAPL ) and Alphabet 's ( GOOGL ) Google are another positive for the stock, he said.
"For Netflix, mobile app store billing may be a small portion of revenue at current, but this mix will rise as the company pushes further into large mobile-first markets like India, Indonesia, etc.," he said.
Investment bank Barclays has a different take. It sees Netflix's efforts to cut out the app store middlemen as a sign of a maturing market.
"The new trend of companies like Fortnite, Netflix, etc., bypassing the 30% app store tax from Google and Apple might be a signal that mobile consumer internet is reaching a saturation point in the West," Barclays analysts said in a report Friday. The trend could mean "that we are moving into a new phase whereby companies are more focused on improving efficiency within their existing business vs. reaching for 'low calorie' growth."
Netflix stock ranks No. 29 on the IBD 50 list of top-performing growth stocks. It has an IBD Composite Rating of 92. That means it has outperformed 92% of stocks in key metrics over the past 12 months.
